notes:
First version.

  • Turn-based trail-bike matches on a square-grid scene: every rider locks in a steer, a gear and an optional boost, then all bikes run at once.
  • Locked moves are held on the GM's client until the round runs, so players cannot read each other's moves.
  • Arena builder: three sizes, five layouts (open floor, pillars, cross, mirrored scatter, and fully random) and four colour schemes. Setup always works on an arena scene, building one if the world has none, so the scene the GM was looking at is never changed by accident. With a setting switched on, any other square-grid scene can be played on as it is, with its walls as barriers.
  • Teams (up to four) or everyone for themselves.
  • Autopilot for GM riders at easy, normal and hard. The GM sees every locked move and can change any of them.
  • Written with Starfinder 2e in mind. Every rider rolls Piloting at the start of each round: a success gives one spare space to use that round, a critical success two.
  • A rider about to wreck rolls Piloting to swerve: a success pulls the bike up short, a critical success keeps its gear. Each swerve after a rider's first in a match is 2 harder. The GM can allow one a match, or none.
  • Piloting rank sets a bike's boost charges. D&D 5e uses Dexterity in Piloting's place; other systems roll flat. Pathfinder 2e is not supported.
  • Rules the GM can set: fading trails, whether a wrecked rider's trail stays, a lock-in timer, and ruling on the match once the sides are walled off (by who would be left running, each bike counted on its own floor).
  • Rider console with hotkeys, a preview of the planned move, and markers for where other bikes could get to.

Full details in the release notes.
